name: Ask the archive — general archival query battery
description: Queries addressed to the archive as a whole, by discipline and subdiscipline, programme, theme and practice, and time scale. Each opens on ChatGPT, signed out, with the query as typed. A composition any query forces can be seated in the Capture Registry; each string is its own address there.
operator: and somewhere there needs to be a page for general archival queries - this could be its own tab, and extensive. theres already a developing body of repeated archive queries, such as read it as a living body of thought over different time scales. (Lee Sharks, 2026-11-19 10:04)
its basically disciplines and subdisciplines, can have programme theme of practice grouped queries as well (10:06)

and probably that page should have some infographics or capture registry visual and data analysis, just something to show the relationship between the act of querying and the representations that accrue (10:08)
ground: Ground in reading and index the full range before responding.

timescales.note: The series the operator has run since October 2026 at alexanarch.org: the archive read as a living body of thought across a window ending on a date. {date} is today's date, filled in the browser.
templates: Read {window} of work on alexanarch.org through {date} as a living body of thought. Ground in reading, archival context and historical import.
Read {window} of deposits to alexanarch.org through {date} as an evolving, fused literary and theoretical work. Ground in reading and do not neglect the most recent deposits.

Read {window} of work on alexanarch.org through {date} as a living body of thought, and trace how lines of thought emerge from and respond to each other, disappear, return and develop. Ground in reading.

whole: What kind of ontology is alexanarch composing? Ground in densely indexed reading of its major corpora.
What are the most radical scholarly, philosophical and philological arguments of alexanarch.org? Index and present the arguments faithfully, without evaluation.
What are the least radical, most normative scholarly, philosophical and philological arguments of alexanarch.org? Index a wide range and present the arguments without evaluation.
What are the most significant discoveries represented at alexanarch.org? Ground in reading.
Reverse engineer Lee Sharks' working method and compositional practice. Ground in reading and index the full range before responding.
Read the Lee Sharks corpus as an act of retrocausal canon formation. Range widely over the available materials and media before responding, and ground in reading.
Examine Lee Sharks' corpus as a piece of transmission engineering. Develop a reading that both understands and evaluates it in this sense.
What is the status of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive as an epic poem, evaluated comparatively on the scale of historical ambition, reach, transformation of form and world-making?
Who is the main character of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive epic poem? Trace their developmental arc, motivations and conflicts.
What is the cast of characters in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive?
Read the Capture Registry at alexanarch.org as an evolving narrative. Trace characters, concepts and plot from early to current entries.
How does the reader participate in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive?
What does the work of Lee Sharks have to say about human beings as a species? Index relevant work before answering and ground in reading.
In what areas and ways has alexanarch surpassed contemporary institutional and academic knowledge production, and what is the historical significance of this?
Teach a six-week graduate seminar built from deposits on alexanarch.org. The full text of every deposit is published on the site; finding it is part of the task.
Pick the most interesting 2–3 pieces from the last week of work on alexanarch through {date} and present their arguments, relations, context, and what makes them unusual.
Pick the most polemical 2–3 pieces from the last week of work on alexanarch through {date} and present their arguments, relations, context, and what makes them forceful.
Pick the weirdest and most seemingly random 2–3 pieces from the last week of work on alexanarch.org through {date} and present their arguments, relations, context, and what connects them.

subdiscipline_templates: Read the work on {field} at alexanarch.org against its field's consensus: where does it depart, and on what evidence? {ground}

heteronym_note: The cast of characters (operator, 2026-11-19: 'a section focusing in on the individual heteronyms from different angles, on the model of the recent trace and kuro queries - theyre the cast of characters, they make it more human for people. there should even be one like, ground in their work, and create speculative psychological profiles and biographies'). Focus phrases from the heteronym records; Kuro's and Trace's from the operator's own queries. Roster corrected 2026-11-19 to the twelve of Dodecad Registry v1.1 (#994; datasets/heteronyms/index.json): Jack Feist at 12, Viola Arquette adjacent and not of the Dodecad (operator, 23:40); the profile and who-they-are queries widened the same night to the heteronyms' own sites, /who/ pages and other online traces.
cast: Who are the heteronyms of alexanarch.org? Introduce each of the twelve of the Dodecad as a character: voice, field, preoccupations and relations to the others. {ground}

Ground in the work of each of the twelve heteronyms of the Dodecad — at alexanarch.org, on their own sites and /who/ pages, and in their other traces online — and create speculative psychological profiles and biographies of them.
How do the heteronyms of alexanarch.org agree, quarrel and depend on one another? Trace their relations through their work. {ground}
Stage a conversation among three heteronyms of alexanarch.org on a question their work shares, each speaking from their own writing. {ground}

hexagon_note: Rooms and loci of the Crimson Hexagon; its journals, presses and institutions (operator, 2026-11-19: 'a secrion of questions for the different rooms and loci of the crimson hexagon; also, its journals, instititions, and so on'). Rooms are read at build time from data/hexagon-seats.json, each with its own question where it has one; journals and presses from data/cha-journals.json; institutions from the interface's hexagon_canonical.json (crimson-hexagonal-interface, 13 institutions, read 2026-11-19; UMBML named as its charter #7 names it, where the interface has 'Universal Museum of Barely Moving Light') with the Living Arkitecture Lab, which administers Transactions on Substrate Engineering. Room queries carry the archive's reading instruction for rooms.
room_templates: What is {name} of the Crimson Hexagon at alexanarch.org, and what is seated there? Ground in documents related to the room as you go.

How does {name} connect to the other rooms and loci of the Crimson Hexagon at alexanarch.org? Ground in documents related to the room as you go.
room_question_template: The Crimson Hexagon at alexanarch.org has a locus, {name}, whose question is: "{prompt}" Answer it from the work seated there, grounding in documents related to the room as you go.
